title: Dead Sea Scrolls
summary: A large collection of ancient Jewish manuscripts discovered in caves near Qumran.
historical_context: The scrolls are foundational evidence for textual transmission and Jewish diversity in the late Second Temple period.
ancient_near_east_context: The item belongs to the broader imperial, cultic, and urban world of the ancient Near East and the biblical periods reflected in the dataset.
literary_context: Important for the textual history of the Hebrew Bible and Second Temple Judaism.
covenantal_significance: Dead Sea Scrolls helps anchor biblical claims in historical reality while reminding readers that archaeology supports rather than replaces interpretation.
interpretive_notes: The discovery is secure, but the social identity of the Qumran community remains debated.
